title: Deeper/broader cross-language DXF writer invariants and bounded test readiness
mode: primary-source web research and plan-only refinement
scope: Screen a newly surfaced cross-language DXF writer for reusable writer-test invariants
Compare declared whole-output writer checks with current local hardening-test coverage
Refine only the existing PAR-12/S13 writer-hardening checkpoint while preserving fast per-slice validation

method.kind: Read-only review of current public project documentation and local test sources
method.limitations: The Go writer statements are mutable-branch maintainer documentation and were not independently executed. This review establishes a test-design lead only, not a libdxfrw defect, interoperability result, or format rule.

sources.revision: Mutable default branch README reviewed 2026-10-18; no GitHub release listed
sources.observed: The README describes a narrow R2010/AC1024 Go writer with LINE, CIRCLE, ARC, LWPOLYLINE and TEXT, no reader, and no block/paper-space or advanced-entity support. It documents group-pair parsing, unique handles, owner closure, mandatory tables, ordered sections, exact golden bytes, and a fuzz invariant that rejects invalid models or emits complete pairs ending in EOF.

sources.revision: Mutable master source and manual reviewed 2026-10-18
sources.observed: The project documents route-specific fuzz entry points; dwgrewrite contains a decode→encode→decode harness. This is useful crash/robustness methodology, not an independent semantic oracle.

The documentation distinguishes ordinary strict reads for structurally sound drawings from recovery for flawed input, and exposes raw browsing separately from loaded-model inspection. This supports separate structural, semantic, recovery, and native-acceptance outcomes.

sources.revision: Working-tree source at baseline commit de27a3391a624aba03ca71f3583c4b3a6e6396a9
sources.observed: tests/hardening_tests.cpp has deterministic DXF and DWG reader fuzz-smoke entry points. Repository search found no writer-output fuzz/property target. Existing writer tests provide numerous focused byte/tag, graph, failure-atomicity, and retry controls; absence of a broad output property target is not itself a serialization defect.

assessment.planImpact: Adds one bounded, optional generated writer-output property check under existing PAR-12/S13. It checks complete framing through terminal EOF, handle/owner closure, and unchanged-destination refusal/retry. It runs only at the existing scheduled writer-hardening checkpoint or when generic writer framing/transaction logic changes; it does not add per-slice full suites, peer/native execution, fixtures, dependencies, or support claims.

implementationReadyChecks: Generate small valid typed graphs and nearby invalid cases in memory; cap test cases, entity counts, and output bytes.

For ASCII and Binary DXF success cases, use a minimal framing scan independent of writer internals to check complete code/value pairs, balanced sections, one terminal group-0 EOF, unique handles, and role-correct owner/reference closure.
For refusal cases, seed the destination with sentinel bytes; verify no replacement or append, then repair and retry through the same writer/output path.
Keep exact field semantics in the existing golden/vector tests; do not promote framing success, self-readback, or the peer's self-described coverage percentage to semantic support.

Reuse an existing hardening/writer target and do not add a CTest registration. Run the focused selector only when generic framing/validation/transaction/handle allocation changes or at a scheduled hardening checkpoint.
Do not add coverage-guided writer mutation unless the deterministic property check demonstrates a named state-space gap; any later campaign must be opt-in, scratch-only, bounded, and locally seeded.
Retain the fixture policy: no peer/customer files and no fuzz-generated DXF fixtures are committed.
